sections.text: As the ignorant act, because of their fondness for action, so should the wise act without such attachment, fixing their eyes, O Arjuna, only on the welfare of the world.

But a wise man should not perturb the minds of the ignorant, who are attached to action; let him perform his own actions in the right spirit, with concentration on Me, thus inspiring all to do the same.
Action is the product of the Qualities inherent in Nature. It is only the ignorant man who, misled by personal egotism, says: I am the doer.

We had been discussing chapter three, Karma Yoga and so far we have seen that act you must, because that is the nature of the Prakriti and you are part of the Prakriti. And Prakriti is maintained by each others actions. And since you are part of that, you have a duty to perform your part in the Prakriti.
How long do I have to continue performing these actions? Bhagavan said, as long as you are identified with the Prakriti. As long as I consider this body, mind and intellect to be me, I have to continue performing Niyata Karma, the karmas that are ordained by the roles which I take as part of this Prakriti. So when I say this is me and now I take the role, I have duties to be performed.
But when I get out of this identification with this Prakriti which is right now, this body, mind and intellect and identify with the self, then there is no action. Bhagawan says for such a person, one who is reveling in the self is satisfied with the self. For such a person there is no action because he does not have anything to gain which he not have gained already.
Once I get out of this identification with the limited self and identify with this supreme self, there is nothing to be gained, nothing to be competing against, and nothing that I have to do to achieve what Im trying to achieve right now, which is a complete bliss and a complete happiness. Because that the very nature of the self, the very nature of the self is Sat chit and Ananda. Right now Im trying to get out of this mortality.
Im 66, and my life insurance goes till 80. It will be better if I die before 80, because all these premiums I have paid all this life will be in vain if I die one day after 80. So I can see my mortality.
People ask me, when are you going to retire? I say I have no plan. But then I say, I am already 66. In the next 5 years I will be 71 -- will I be able to function? So whether I like it or not, I am bound by mortality.
And what Im trying to do is overcome that mortality. Im seeing myself as mortal. Im trying to become Sat -- ever existing.
I always find myself to be not knowledgeable enough. I dont know everything that I need to know. So Im constantly in the quest for learning more and more and more -- that is Chit.
The very nature of the self is all knowing. So theres nothing more to be known. And right now all Im trying to get out of is the unhappy unconducive situation.
So I will be in Ananda once I realize thats my true nature. As long as youre identified with this Prakriti, you have to be bound by the laws of Prakriti -- that every constituent part has to function to make the Prakriti function. And therefore as long as you identified with the Prakrutti, you have to do your part.
Once you identify with this self, none of the laws of Prakrutti are applicable to you. Prakrutti will sustain by itself. Thats not your responsibility.
Because you say, Okay, Im satisfied with the self and I dont act -- then who will? Thats the one question everybody has. Who will do all these things which are happening in this world? He said, thats not your problem. Prakriti will take care of itself.
You are in trouble right now. You are in pain right now of this unhappiness. You want to get out of it.
Once you get out of this identification, you have nothing else to do. There is no action for such a person. Say, till that time what am I supposed to do? Asaktaha Karya Samacha.
Till that time, you continue working, performing all your Niyata Karma. Except right now you are performing with attachment -- People will recognize me, at least if I do something for my family, my family will say youre doing good -- Im doing it out of attachment. He said, just do without attachment.
Continue doing what you are doing. Except Asaktah Karma Samachara, you do all your action without attachment. With that minor adjustment in what you are doing, you will achieve that perfection.
Many people in the past, Janak Adayah Janak and others Karma Nai vahi samsiddhaha, they have achieved this just by performing their actions diligently without any attachment. And they achieve the perfection. So could you, so should you.
And then he said, now if I have come to the conclusion that I have done everything, that I really dont have to achieve anything, then what should I do? Still continue to act in this world, at least for the Loka Sangraha, for the welfare of the society. Once I come to the conclusion that I have achieved everything I have achieved, you continue to contribute your contribution to the society, for the welfare of the society. Thats because the same poison which you have right now, of your own ego, once you take that and dilute it, right now this ego is identified with this limited self.
I call me this body, mind and intellect. I take this ego and dilute it with a larger arena, it will lose its bite. At a 1985 camp, at the end of it, there was a question-answer session.
Somebody asked, do you have ego? What could be the answer?, of course I have ego. He said, without ego, how can I control all of you? And now what we think is, if he has ego, I have ego. So what is the difference between you and I? Why am I wasting my one week and all these dollars to come here and spend time here? Then the second part of his answer is always is what comes out as the real answer.
Yes, I have ego, and so should you. Because without ego, you cannot function. Without any identification, no activity can take place.
However, when you take that ego and dilute it. So say you take a pinch of salt and put it in a cup of water and you taste the water, it will be salty. You take the same water and put it in a jar of water.
That salt will not be that noticeable. You take that same jar of water and put it into a whole pond of water. That salt is nowhere to be found.
It is still there, so diluted in this body of water that that salt is not effective anymore. Same ego which is right now is so bothersome to me. When I take it and apply it to a larger group of people, it becomes manageable.
When I identify with my family, it is much more manageable. When I identify with my community, its even more manageable. I identify with my nation, I become a patriot, I become a hero.
When I identify with the whole cosmos, Bhagavan said, you become the realized person. So he said, those who are satisfied with the self, by the self, they have no action other than those. All of your actions, how long? As long as you identify with it.
And then he said, even after you realize that, you have to still continue to work for the Loka Sangraha, for the benefit of society. Now hes giving his own example. So one who has realized what the reality of life is.
Yadi aham na varteyam jatum karmani atandritah Mama vartmanuvartante manusyaha partha sarvasah. We also seen that Yatyat Acharati sreshta tattat eva itarojanah. It is the very nature of our being that we need something to follow.
Some role model, some standard to follow. So someone becomes a role model in our life. Our parents, our teacher, our three year old granddaughter.
She comes to me and says, Dada, lets do numbers. So well put numbers on the floor. And I say, Okay, now Ill ask you. She says, No, no, Ill ask you -- show me number five. So obviously Ill say, But Medha, how about I ask you? No, no, no -- show me number five. So then Ill purposely show number six and say, Thats number five. Thats not number five! See, she mimics her teacher. She sees what happens in her class, and she wants to practice on Meena.
She doesnt want to be a student here -- she wants to be the teacher. She actually does exactly what her teacher does. Because we have a tendency to follow the behavior we find attractive.
So Yatyat acharyati sreshta Purusha. So you have to set a standard of your behavior. Because people are going to follow you whether you like it or not.
Because you are role model to somebody. And therefore he says, even when you reach the highest state where there is no action left for you, you have to continue working. Because I as the supreme being, once we realize the self, he becomes the one with him.
If I stop working, other people will follow my example. Other beings will follow my example and they will stop working also. Mama vartmanu vartanti manusyaha partha sarvasaram. We said that Rama took Avatara to set standards for us.
What is the standard for good son? What is the standard for a good husband? What is the standard of a good king? What is the standard of a good father? He came to demonstrate what model behavior is. We may or may not agree with him on certain things. So Ramayana is Acharaniya.
Everything Rama did is to be followed. Krishna, on the other hand, is not Acharaniya at all. What he did, you cannot do.
Because he did the dance on Kaliya Nag, we cannot do that. And therefore you also cannot have 1,008 or whatever wives he had. So we have to set a role model.
When we become the Supreme, we still have a role to play. If I dont do my role, other people will stop. Utsideyuh Ime Lokah Na Kuryam Karma Chet Aham -- if I stop working or acting, this world will perish.
So now I think we come to the conclusion that Krishna is not talking about himself as Devakis son. Because the world did not stop working after Krishna was gone. Its still going on.
He is speaking as the first person singular, as the Self which is all-pervading. The Creator and the controller of this universe. If that stops functioning, this world will perish.
This world is functioning as a cosmos and not as chaos because it has laws. We all know there are laws of nature. No denying because we can test it right now.
Go on a second floor and jump out of the window. The laws which Newton found out are still very valid after all these years. So there are laws in nature and then laws are enforced.
So he remains the lawgiver and law enforcer, and he does not take a day off. If he takes a day off and the laws are mixed up that day, the world will be in chaos. Imagine the laws of thermodynamics working Monday through Friday but stopping on Saturday.
Sunday takes a weekend. I wouldnt be able to come here because the car wont start. So he said without taking any break, I have to continue working because this world will only function.
The Prakriti will only follow the laws if I am there to support these laws. Sankrasi Chakarta Syam Upahanyami Imaha Prajaha. This teaching connects to our dharma and duty, which we sometimes find difficult because of our cultural burden and the complexity of the caste system inherited from hundreds of years.

These verses contain a crucial teaching for anyone who has gained spiritual understanding: do not disturb the minds of others who are still attached to their actions. The wise person (vidvan) should work alongside the ignorant (avidvan), performing the same actions but with a different inner attitude. This is not hypocrisy - it is compassion. Abruptly telling someone immersed in worldly pursuits that all action is bondage may paralyze rather than liberate them.
The revelation in verse 27 is equally important: Prakriteh kriyamanani gunaih karmani sarvashah - all actions are performed by the gunas of Prakriti (nature). It is only the ego-deluded person (ahankara-vimudhatma) who thinks I am the doer. This is a fundamental shift in perspective. You are not the doer; the qualities of nature - sattva, rajas, and tamas - are interacting with each other. Your body-mind is an instrument through which these forces operate.
Today, practice observing your actions as the play of the gunas rather than the products of I. When you feel energetic and clear, recognize sattva at work. When you feel driven and restless, see rajas. When you feel dull and resistant, observe tamas. Instead of saying I am lazy or I am productive, try saying Tamas is predominant right now or Rajas is active. This subtle shift dissolves the grip of ego on action. Also, consider: Is there someone in your life who is earnestly engaged in their work, even if with attachment? Rather than correcting their philosophy, can you inspire them by your example of engaged yet detached action?
